question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend abstraction now, and which first slice should own provider scope, credential isolation, private-network policy, and fallback behavior?
rationale: Current source proves the capability is missing, but the safe implementation crosses native apps, Gateway/provider contracts, settings, secrets, privacy, and network policy.

options.title: Start With macOS PTT Seam
options.body: Use the narrower macOS Push-to-Talk slice to define a batch STT backend contract while preserving Apple Speech as the default and reusing Gateway/media provider policy where feasible.

options.title: Design Broad Cross-Platform ASR
options.body: Plan one provider/config surface across macOS, iOS, Android, and WebChat, accepting a larger product and security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer Native ASR
options.body: Keep self-hosted STT limited to current `tools.media.audio`, Talk relay, channel, and sidecar paths until maintainers prioritize native-app extension points.

recommendation.title: Start With macOS PTT Seam
recommendation.body: Use the narrower macOS Push-to-Talk slice to define a batch STT backend contract while preserving Apple Speech as the default and reusing Gateway/media provider policy where feasible.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily product-scope for native voice behavior, and steipete has the clearest feature-history signal for Talk/native voice direction.
